sm: Ben Shapiro opens by contrasting two images of Sophia Hernandez-Mihia, a Seattle-area woman who is not in the country legally. In June she wore a jersey at a World Cup event that blended Palestinian and Mexican themes, and last weekend she was filmed screaming and crying as she was deported to Mexico. He says the turntables have turned, and suggests it may be time to deport people who do not like American civilization.

Shapiro says there has been talk over the past two days about amnesty. He returns to Hernandez-Mihia, who arrived from Mexico as a teenager on a tourist visa, pursued citizenship through marriage, and was arrested for allegedly throwing hot coffee at ICE agents. He argues she praised Mexico until she had to live there. He then turns to Hugh Hewitt, who wrote a Fox News piece urging a presidential pardon or regularization for a defined group of illegal immigrants, such as people here ten years or more with no felonies and steady employment. Shapiro says he sees the political logic if Democrats may take power, but he rejects the claim that the public wants mass amnesty. He asks why the government can audit millions of taxpayers yet cannot screen illegal immigrants for criminality, welfare dependence, or anti-American activity. He also notes a House Democratic bill that would end removal orders left unenforced for ten years.

Shapiro says Americans do not favor broad amnesty and that Hewitt's standards are too permissive, since people can meet them while drawing welfare or leaving children dependent on taxpayers. Anyone who helps America, he says, should still go to the back of the line. He then cites a New York Post report on a Honduran man arrested 38 times in New York City, released without bail by a judge the day before he allegedly murdered a 62-year-old woman. He criticizes Zohran Mamdani for dodging a question on whether the man should have been freed.

He argues Democrats will always outbid Republicans on immigration and are soft on crime, citing Hasan Piker calling himself a law and order Democrat and an LA DSA board member calling for the deaths of tech executives. He also criticizes Ms. Rachel for visiting an immigration court and speaking about conditions for detained children, and quotes the White House press secretary's response. He concludes that a blanket amnesty would not win votes and is bad policy. He then says some native-born citizens should lose citizenship, pointing to the legal grounds for renouncing it.

Shapiro describes Sneako, a 28-year-old streamer named Nick Lizzick who moved into the manosphere, converted to Islam, and endorsed Mamdani. Sneako says he was questioned for eight hours by US agents after meeting Taliban members in Afghanistan. Shapiro says that was appropriate and that he may not deserve to return. He plays clips of Sneako telling the Taliban the West created them, and of him apparently eating pork by accident. His conclusion is that people who hate America, born here or not, can leave, and that the populist position on immigration is to shut the border and admit only those who will integrate.

Shapiro then covers what he calls the stupid controversy of the day at Austin Peay State University. Students were upset over a supposed noose on campus that turned out to be a shoelace in a tree, and a male student later turned himself in to police. He mocks the university statement that it has no tolerance for such acts and says students seem to be looking for an excuse to feel victimized. He compares the protest reaction to Selma and says it is a manufactured controversy.

Shapiro says this victim mentality has spread through culture, citing Jennifer Lopez telling the New York Times she struggled to get roles because she was not a typical white actress. He contrasts her with Darius Rucker, who said he was told his country music career was impossible and did it anyway. He says racism and bigotry come from many directions, then plays Justice Sonia Sotomayor saying society should focus on how it understands things. He contrasts that with a justice at the American Enterprise Institute arguing for race neutrality in admissions, and he doubts the public will stand for it.

Shapiro turns to Nvidia and whether it tacitly allowed restricted chips to reach China through Singapore firms such as Megaspeed. Singapore's prime minister said the chips never entered Singapore, and reports cite at least 7.5 billion dollars in chips shipped to Chinese companies. He says Democrats like Ruben Gallego will subpoena devices and records and are eager to attack. He also replies to Democrats saying Republicans can no longer criticize socialism over government stakes in companies like Intel. He closes by mocking Sunny Hostin's claim that Hillary Clinton has never been wrong, and says the big question is what Nvidia knew and when.

Shapiro calls the White House turkey pardon the dumbest tradition, then plays President Trump pardoning two turkeys and declaring they will live forever. He turns to the Boston City Council's recognition of a National Day of Mourning, in which speakers describe Thanksgiving as an injustice to Indigenous peoples. He says every society has a brutal past, including slavery everywhere, and the difference is that Americans consider those wrongs bad and fought a civil war over them.

He then goes through questions from subscribers about dealing with liberal relatives at Thanksgiving. Skipping politics is fine, he says. If a cousin claims the midterms vindicated Medicare for all, he says Democrats won because of corruption concerns, the Iran war fallout, and chaos, and that a king with real power could not have been defied. To a doomsday cousin he says keep a stash of supplies, but doomsday is not coming. To abolish-ICE advocates he says be specific about who enforces immigration law, and he argues life begins at conception.

He also asks a brother-in-law who calls him Islamophobic to name a free Muslim-governed state. He says small Muslim populations are not a problem but large ones are, and that no such state shares Western values. He adds that wealth does not make people unethical, it only makes them more of what they are. For conspiracy theorists, he says to get up and watch football.
sg: Thanksgiving Pardons and Family Dinner Debates
